_comment: Seeds for the Sharp Tracker manager-discovery graph. Sleeper publishes no global user or league directory, so the cohort can only grow OUTWARD from leagues we already know. Add a league here whenever you join one — the crawl picks it up on the next run with no code change.
_seedVsSignal: A seed league does NOT have to be a dynasty league. Seeds exist to find USERS; only dynasty/keeper leagues feed the transaction ledger (src/intel/league_filter.py). A large redraft tournament is one of the best user sources available precisely because it puts many unrelated managers in one place — its trades are simply never counted.

seedLeagues.name: The Megalabowl
seedLeagues.note: Redraft (settings.type=0) — DISCOVERY ONLY, never counted in the dynasty signal. 13 members, each of whom plays in unrelated leagues, which is what makes it a high-yield seed.

seedUsers.note: Platform owner. Their current leagues are re-read every run, so newly joined leagues enter the graph automatically.

Curated industry sharp (Final 100 workbook), promoted to a verified identity by explicit admin review on 2026-08-04 — see sharp_review_decisions for the audit row. Seeded because the movement ledger is empty and a wider seed set is the only thing that fills it; an industry analyst's league portfolio reaches managers the owner's own leagues never touch. Public unauthenticated traversal only, same call budget and inter-call sleep as every other seed. Being a seed confers nothing: whether his trades COUNT is decided at read time by the qualified-cohort filter, not by appearing here.

traversal._comment: BFS outward: league -> members -> their leagues -> those leagues' members -> ... Generation 0 is the seed set.
traversal._rateLimitNote: Sleeper documents 'stay under 1000 API calls per minute'. 0.12s between calls is ~500/min, deliberately half the stated ceiling.

limits._comment: Backstops so a runaway traversal cannot spend an unbounded crawl. Reaching one is reported, never silent.
